title: Pairs Bounded by Sum and Difference
statement:
You get an integer array nums. For indexes i < j, let a = nums[i] and b = nums[j]. The pair is bounded when both of these hold:

  • min(|a − b|, |a + b|) ≤ min(|a|, |b|)
  • max(|a − b|, |a + b|) ≥ max(|a|, |b|)

Return how many index pairs are bounded.

examples.why: With a 0 and a 4, min(4, 4) = 4 is not ≤ 0. Two zeros give 0 ≤ 0 and 0 ≥ 0, so only that pair counts.
(-6, 6), (-6, 12) and (6, 12) count. Signs do not matter here: -6 and 6 behave the same. The -1 is too small next to any of them.

hints: Try a few numbers with different signs. Do the signs of a and b ever change the answer?
With x = |a| and y = |b|, the two expressions |a − b| and |a + b| are always |x − y| and x + y in some order. Rewrite both conditions with x and y.
The second condition always holds. The first becomes: the larger absolute value is at most twice the smaller. Sort the absolute values and count with two pointers.

explain.intuition:
Signs only decide which of |a − b| and |a + b| is the bigger one. If a and b share a sign, the difference is small; otherwise the sum is. Either way, with x = |a| and y = |b|, the smaller one is |x − y| and the larger one is x + y.

Now the second condition, x + y ≥ max(x, y), is always true. The first, |x − y| ≤ min(x, y), says: with x ≥ y, x ≤ 2y. So count pairs of absolute values where the bigger is at most twice the smaller. After sorting, for each value as the bigger one, the valid partners to its left form a contiguous block, and its left edge only moves right. That is a two-pointer sweep.
steps: Replace every number with its absolute value and sort ascending.
Keep a left pointer lo = 0. For each j, move lo right while 2·v[lo] < v[j].
Every index in lo … j − 1 pairs with j: add j − lo.
pitfalls: Keeping the signs and sorting raw values. -6 and 12 are a valid pair even though they sit far apart when sorted by value.
Forgetting that zero pairs only with zero: x ≤ 2·0 forces x = 0.
Storing the count in a 32-bit integer. With 100 000 equal values there are almost 5·10⁹ pairs.

solutions.title: Check every pair with the raw definition
solutions.idea: Evaluate both conditions exactly as written for every i < j.

solutions.title: Sorted absolute values and binary search
solutions.idea: The condition is max ≤ 2·min on absolute values. Sort them, and for each value binary-search the first value that is at least half of it.

solutions.title: Sorted absolute values and two pointers
solutions.idea: As the bigger value grows, the smallest valid partner only moves right, so one forward-only pointer replaces the binary search.

followups: Change the rule to max ≤ 3·min. Which line of the solution changes?
Answer many queries: how many bounded pairs lie inside nums[l..r]? What would you precompute?
